observability._note: OpenConnector adopts the OpenRegister AppHost observability engine (ADR-040). These descriptors reproduce the output of the now-deleted hand-written HealthController + MetricsController. The /api/health and /api/metrics routes are aliased to AppHost\Controller\GenericHealth#index / GenericMetrics#index (registered in lib/AppInfo/Application.php with appName=openconnector), so the engine reads this block at request time. Parity: metric names, types and label keys match the pre-adoption contract. Intentional improvements: /api/health is now #[PublicPage] and returns 503 on a failed database check (ADR-006); the bespoke `sources_table` OR-join probe is subsumed by the generic `openregister` availability check (degraded). POST-CUTOVER FLIP (done): the 9 counted descriptors used to be tableCount over the chain-C legacy openconnector_* tables. Those tables are gone — every entity is an OpenRegister object — so all 9 had been exporting HELP+TYPE and ZERO samples ever since the cutover, which reads identically to a genuinely idle instance and is exactly why it went unnoticed. They are now objectCount over register `openconnector` and the schema that replaced each table. The UNGROUPED ones are plain objectCount and are correct — measured live: jobs_total 18, mappings_total 19, synchronizations_total 18, endpoints_total 0, rules_total 0, where before the flip all five emitted nothing. The three LABELLED ones (sources_total, calls_total, synchronization_runs_total) are `provider` instead, computed in lib/Observability/OpenConnectorMetricsProvider.php, for two measured reasons: (1) objectCount's GROUPED path emits nothing even when the data is there — `getFacetsForObjects()` returned no terms buckets for a plain JSON property, so sources_total produced zero samples against 22 Sources all carrying type="api" (the pre-existing traces_total has the same symptom); (2) object sources have no labelMap, so the label would read `statusCode`/`result` rather than the `status` the spec mandates, and expandGroups() drops zero buckets so the spec's zero-value placeholder scenarios are inexpressible. Both filed as ConductionNL/openregister#2308. job_runs_total stays declarative and groups by `level` — the job_log schema has no status property at all, and no requirement asserts its labels. NOTE: ProviderMetricSource ignores its descriptor and returns EVERY provider sample for EACH provider descriptor, so provider families are currently rendered once per provider descriptor; that duplication is the same upstream issue.

config._note: PURPOSE: A source is an external system OpenConnector calls (REST/SOAP/DB/file). This is the CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype — an integrator lands here to check whether the connection is healthy and to triage failed calls, not to read documents. DESIGN RATIONALE: the body leads with operational data. Four KPI stats across the top (total calls, errors, avg size, objects fetched) give an at-a-glance health read; the primary body region is a recent-call-log table (child call_log filtered by source UUID = @objectId, sorted newest-first) because triaging HTTP failures is the #1 job on this page. Connection config (data, 3 columns to fit the many auth/rate-limit fields) and Related sit below/beside. NO comms leaves — a source does not email or hold meetings; the schema declares no email/calendar linkedType. Rarely-opened raw JSON blobs (paths/headers/loggingConfig) stay in the sidebar metadata, and audit-trail is a sidebar tab. ADR-062 rev3: the four health KPIs (calls, errors, objects fetched, avg payload) live in ONE in-grid stats-block top-right of the Connection core-data widget — entries[] carries per-entry metric/field so the sum (objectCount) and avg (size, raw bytes via countLabel) are expressible alongside the two counts. Registry icons; call log is read-only (allowCreate:false) with a View-all to SourceLogs.

content.emptyText: No calls logged for this source yet.

widgets.title: Environments

content.emptyText: This source is not used as a promotion environment.

widgets._note: Environments moved here from their own top-level index. The `environment` schema carries NO connection or credential material of its own — just name/slug/role plus `sourceRef` pointing at the `source` (type: api) that holds the location and credentialRef. So an environment is an attribute OF a source, and listing it beside the source it points at is where an operator can actually act on it. Promotion is not a daily operation, which is why it stopped being a top-level menu entry. Icon is 'Earth' from the SHARED widget registry (nextcloud-vue widgetIcons.js), not the menu vocabulary: an unregistered widget icon renders the '?' fallback (ADR-062 rule 8). ServerNetwork, the obvious name, is not in that registry.

config._note: PURPOSE: An endpoint is an inbound route OpenConnector exposes (path + HTTP method) that maps requests onto a target (register/schema/source/job) via input/output mappings and attached rules. CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype. DESIGN RATIONALE: unlike a source, an endpoint has NO child log table with an endpoint foreign key (call_log keys on source/synchronization, not endpoint), so there is no runs list to surface — the operational payload IS the routing configuration. The body therefore leads with a wide config panel (data, 2 columns) exposing path/regex, method, targetType/targetId and the input/output mapping references, with a Related panel beside it so the integrator can jump to the mappings and target this endpoint wires together. NO comms leaves — an endpoint routes HTTP, it does not communicate; the schema declares no email/calendar linkedType. The verbose conditions[]/rules[]/endpointArray JSON stays reachable in sidebar metadata; audit-trail is a sidebar tab.

PURPOSE: A consumer is an external client authorised to call OpenConnector (auth type + allowed domains/IPs). CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype. DESIGN RATIONALE: the two things an admin does here are (1) confirm the access policy and (2) see what this consumer has actually been sent. The body pairs a compact access-config panel (data, 2 columns: authorizationType, domains, ips) with a Related panel, then leads the lower body with an event-delivery table — event_message rows filtered by the consumer UUID (@objectId), newest-first, showing status/retries/last-attempt — because delivery health is the operational signal for a subscribed consumer. Two KPI stats (deliveries, failed) sit up top. NO comms leaves — a consumer is a machine client, not a person; the schema declares no email/calendar linkedType. Audit-trail is a sidebar tab. ADR-062 rev3: deliveries+failed are ONE in-grid stats-block (entries[]) top-right of the access-policy core-data widget, each entry deep-linking into EventDeliveries filtered on this consumer. event_message list is read-only (allowCreate:false) with a View-all to EventDeliveries; registry icons.

pages.title: API Products
pages._note: PURPOSE: an api_product is a named, versioned bundle of existing Endpoints a Consumer can subscribe to at a rate-limit tier (api-product-gateway REQ-APG-001/002). Plain generic index — browsing/create/delete needs no bespoke chrome; the endpoint picker, tier editor, analytics panel, and subscription approve/reject actions all live on the custom ApiProductDetail page instead (design.md/discovery.md: 'a plain index for browsing').

Custom detail page for one api_product: endpoint picker (add/remove existing Endpoints), named-tier editor (rateLimit/quota/requiresApproval/approverGroup), the gateway analytics panel (request count, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency via GET /api/products/{id}/analytics), and pending subscriptions with approve/reject actions — a generic OR CRUD detail page can't express any of these (api-product-gateway REQ-APG-002/007, design.md 'it will be custom, mirroring ApprovalDetail').
pages.title: API Product
Webhooks
pages._note: A webhook is an EventSubscription with a delivery sink URL (push/pull). The register has no separate 'webhook' schema — per ADR-013 the EventSubscription entity (sink + protocol + style) IS the webhook. addLabel overrides the schema-title-derived default so the create button reads 'Add Webhook' rather than 'Add EventSubscription'.

pages._note: Custom page: abonnement CRUD backed by the dedicated NotificatiesSubscriberController endpoints (create/update/delete also register/update/delete against the remote ZGW Notificaties API and provision/cascade-delete a companion consumer) — not the generic OR object CRUD a CnIndexPage drives. See notificaties-api-subscriber REQ-008.
Custom page: the mapping editor is a bespoke 3-tab rules editor (mapping/cast/unset rules with drag-reorder + per-rule dialogs) that the generic detail page cannot express.
pages.title: Mapping

pages._note: Custom page: the rule editor renders condition/action configuration with type-specific forms (mapping, error, sync, fetch-extra, write-back) beyond the generic detail page.
pages.title: Rule
Synchronization
pages._note: Custom page: the synchronization editor composes source/target mapping, conditions, follow-ups and run/test controls that the generic detail page cannot express.

config._note: PURPOSE: A CloudEvent is an immutable event record (CloudEvents 1.0 envelope: source/type/subject/specversion + a data payload) that fans out to subscribed consumers. CONFIG/TECHNICAL, read-only archetype — you inspect what happened and where it went, you do not edit it. DESIGN RATIONALE: the body leads with the CloudEvent envelope (data, 2 columns: source/type/subject/time/status) since that is the record itself, then the operational answer to 'was this delivered?' — an event_message table filtered by the event UUID (@objectId) showing each consumer delivery, status and retry count, newest-first. The `data` payload JSON is the second question, so it stays within the data widget (which renders the data field) and the object metadata rather than crowding the body; Related sits beside the envelope. NO comms leaves — a CloudEvent is a technical message record, not a person; the schema declares no email/calendar linkedType and no files are attached.

content.emptyText: No deliveries recorded for this event yet.

pages._note: Custom page: HITL Pending Approvals operations view over approval_request, backed by the two-layer-authorized /api/approvals endpoint (returns only caller-actionable rows) with a status filter and per-row navigation into a detail page whose Approve/Reject verbs hit /api/approvals/{id}/approve|reject. Not the generic OR CRUD a CnIndexPage drives. Mirrors EventDeliveries.
pages.title: Approvals
Flow
pages._note: Custom page: the ordered, reorderable step-list editor (typed rows: type/configRef/condition/onError, plus branch sub-targets) and the manual Run action + run-log tab cannot be expressed by the generic detail page. See visual-flow-orchestration REQ-009. No separate Edit modal — flow metadata (name/description/isEnabled) is edited inline on this page, matching the current RuleDetailPage/SynchronizationDetailPage/MappingDetailPage convention (the legacy src/modals/<Entity>/Edit*.vue modal pattern design.md referenced is unwired dead code post chain-C, per src/handlers/actionHandlers.js's own docblock).
Custom detail page for one approval_request with Approve/Reject actions (reject requires a comment). See hitl-approval-rule-action.
pages.title: Approval request
Traces
pages._note: execution-trace-observability REQ-007: follows the SourceLogs/EndpointLogs/CloudEventLogs `type: logs` precedent — a generic list over execution_trace with server-derived entryPoint/status filters and pagination. Row navigation opens TraceDetail (a custom page — the step timeline and Replay action are not expressible as a generic logs row).

Custom detail page: renders one execution_trace's ordered step timeline (type/duration/status per step, expandable redacted input/output) and a Replay action (dry-run preview shown first; a separate confirmation step is required before a forced replay). Not expressible as a generic detail page — mirrors ApprovalDetail's custom-detail-for-a-custom-verb pattern.
pages.title: Trace
Store
pages._note: ADR-080 store plane: renamed from 'Catalog'. A store is 'browse a registry and install into this instance'; a CATALOGUE is an outward-facing published catalogue (OpenCatalogi's concept) and TEMPLATES are runtime content blueprints. The old name claimed the wrong concept and the old ViewGridOutline glyph is the vocabulary's 'apps' icon, which OpenBuild uses for its Apps page. Card grid over catalog_item, kind-driven quick filters (ADR-080 Decision 5); Enable/Instantiate lives in CatalogItemDetailDialog. Old /catalog route redirects here.

config._configurationUiNote: REQ-006/007/008 Configuration import/export UI actions live here as header actions (ExportConfigurationDialog / ImportPreviewDialog) rather than on a bespoke Configurations index page: OR Configuration groups are a NATIVE OR table (lib/Db/Configuration.php) served by /apps/openregister/api/configurations, not an object register/schema, so a type:index page cannot back them — and a type:custom page is exactly what this change avoids (custom-widget-ratchet).

pages.title: Dead letters
pages._note: Merges the former EventDeliveries (event_message, /api/events/dead-letter) and SyncDeadLetters (sync_item_dead_letter, /api/sync-dead-letter) pages into ONE navigation entry under Operations. They were the same operations view with identical Replay/Discard verbs over two tables — SyncDeadLetters' own note said 'Mirrors EventDeliveries' — and both rendered EmailAlertOutline, so the menu showed one glyph twice. This is a navigation merge, NOT a rewrite: the queues stay separate underneath (different schemas, different admin-only endpoints, different replay semantics) and DeadLettersPage delegates to the two existing components. ?queue=sync deep-links the sync queue, which is where the old /synchronizations/dead-letters route redirects.
